claims.statement: Verb plus scoped outcome plus IF is a validated method for discovering the true binding condition.

estimand.description: Incremental accuracy, completeness, inter-rater agreement and decision usefulness of the IF grammar relative to simpler condition registers.

denominator.description: No representative or preregistered set of service promises, encoders or affected participants has been fixed.

population.description: Intended users and affected populations have not been sampled.

geography.description: No jurisdiction set has been registered for validation.

time.description: No study window or re-test interval has been registered.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: The IF frame is a proposed grammar for generating, challenging and tracking candidate conditions.
prohibited_inferences: The five prompts are complete.
The protocol identifies the true binding condition.
The protocol improves decisions or outcomes.

counterevidence.statement: Completeness, inter-rater reliability, construct validity and decision usefulness have not been tested, and an unregistered viable route can overturn a binding-condition diagnosis.

registered_falsifier.statement: The method hypothesis fails if independent encoders using the IF grammar do not outperform a preregistered simpler assumptions register on material omissions and consequential classification disagreements.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Withdraw diagnostic language if the IF arm fails the preregistered superiority threshold or creates more consequential omissions than the comparator.
evidence_needed: Comparator arm and agreement threshold fixed before results

open_evidence_needs: Preregister and run the ten-service grammar reliability study with an explicit comparator.

claims.statement: The retained processed series reports 44.38% of the world population below 8.30 dollars per day in 2026, expressed in 2021 international dollars.

estimand.description: Modelled share of the represented world population living in households with per-person welfare below 8.30 2021 international dollars per day.

denominator.statistical_unit: persons represented in the source's modelled world population
denominator.description: The world population represented by the processed World Bank-derived series for the 2026 estimate.

population.description: People represented by the source model, subject to its survey coverage and welfare concepts.

geography.description: World aggregate in the processed series.

time.description: 2026 modelled estimate/nowcast as recorded in the retained research, not a direct 2026 census.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: The retained processed World Bank-derived series reports a 2026 modelled estimate of 44.38% below the World Bank 8.30-dollar upper-middle-income line in 2021 PPP.
prohibited_inferences: 44.38% is a direct observation of people alive today.
Everyone below the line cannot access an abundance service.
The estimate identifies any individual's binding condition.

counterevidence.statement: The value is modelled from survey distributions and nowcasting inputs and is not a direct observation or an individual access measure.

registered_falsifier.statement: The source-report claim fails if the frozen source series and metadata do not reproduce 44.38% for the specified threshold, year and PPP vintage.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Withdraw or correct the number if exact reproduction fails; never repair it by changing the threshold, year or vintage after the fact.

open_evidence_needs: Freeze the downloadable source series, metadata, query date and checksum before public use.

claims.statement: The retained processed series reports 80.04% of the world population below a user-set 30-dollar-per-day threshold in 2026, expressed in 2021 international dollars.

estimand.description: Modelled share of the represented world population below a user-selected 30 2021-international-dollar daily welfare threshold.

denominator.statistical_unit: persons represented in the source's modelled world population
denominator.description: The world population represented by the processed World Bank-derived series for the 2026 estimate.

population.description: People represented by the source model, subject to its survey coverage and welfare concepts.

geography.description: World aggregate in the processed series.

time.description: 2026 modelled estimate/nowcast as recorded in the retained research.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: The retained processed series reports a 2026 modelled estimate near four in five below a user-set 30-dollar threshold in 2021 international dollars.
prohibited_inferences: 30 dollars is an official World Bank poverty line.
30 dollars is a validated developed-world floor.
The figure is comparable to nominal-dollar income, GDP or company profit.

counterevidence.statement: The World Bank's published 2021-PPP global poverty lines are 3.00, 4.20 and 8.30 dollars; 30 dollars is a user-set threshold, not an official line or validated developed-world floor.

registered_falsifier.statement: The numerical source-report claim fails if a frozen source series does not reproduce 80.04% for 2026 at the 30-dollar threshold in 2021 international dollars.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Withdraw or correct the number if reproduction fails; keep the threshold explicitly user-selected even if the value reproduces.

open_evidence_needs: Validate any proposed decent-life interpretation against local reference budgets and material deprivation before attaching it to 30 dollars.

claims.statement: Because about four in five people are below the 30-dollar threshold, abundance promises are almost entirely talking to the other fifth.

estimand.description: Relationship between household welfare position and who makes, hears, understands or could benefit from abundance promises.

denominator.statistical_unit: people exposed to a defined corpus of abundance communications
denominator.description: No communication corpus, audience frame or exposure denominator has been registered.

population.description: The population hearing or addressed by abundance rhetoric is not measured by the poverty series.

geography.description: No communication market or jurisdiction is specified.

time.description: No publication or audience-observation period is specified.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: The modelled distribution figures show that affordability constraints are widespread under the selected welfare thresholds.
prohibited_inferences: The figures identify the intended or actual audience of abundance rhetoric.
Income rank determines whether a person can benefit from a named capability.
The lower four fifths share one binding condition.

counterevidence.statement: A population income distribution does not measure the audience, framing, uptake or beneficiaries of abundance communications, so the conclusion is an ecological inference and non sequitur.

registered_falsifier.statement: The audience hypothesis remains withdrawn unless a preregistered content and audience study directly measures which income groups are addressed, reached and able to benefit.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Do not reinstate the claim from distribution data alone; require direct audience and beneficiary evidence for a defined corpus and period.
evidence_needed: Income or welfare measure compatible with the audience sample

open_evidence_needs: No direct audience evidence is retained; remove the claim rather than commission research unless it becomes decision-relevant.

claims.statement: The US Census Bureau estimated that 27.1 million people, 8.0% of the population, had no health insurance coverage at any point during calendar year 2024.

estimand.description: People without health insurance coverage at any point in calendar year 2024 under the CPS ASEC measure; the source also reports the corresponding population percentage.

denominator.statistical_unit: people in the CPS ASEC US population estimate
denominator.description: US population represented by the CPS ASEC annual insurance-coverage estimate.

population.description: People in the United States represented by CPS ASEC.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: Census estimated 27.1 million people, 8.0%, lacked coverage at any point during calendar year 2024 under CPS ASEC.
prohibited_inferences: All uninsured people failed to obtain needed care.
Insured people could afford a named service.
Insurance status was the binding condition for any named patient.

counterevidence.statement: The annual coverage measure does not establish affordability among insured people or access to a particular service.

registered_falsifier.statement: The source-report claim fails if the frozen Census table, definition or correction does not reproduce both 27.1 million and 8.0% for the 2024 annual measure.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Correct or withdraw the number if the frozen official release or a formal correction differs.

open_evidence_needs: Freeze the cited Census PDF and table checksum before public publication.

claims.statement: The 2025 NHIS early release reports that 6.0% of US adults aged 18 or older failed to obtain needed medical care because of cost.

estimand.description: Share of adults aged 18+ who failed to obtain needed medical care due to cost under the 2025 NHIS early-release measure.

denominator.statistical_unit: adults aged 18 or older represented by the 2025 NHIS early release
denominator.description: US adults aged 18+ in the NHIS early-release estimation universe.

population.description: US adults aged 18 or older represented by NHIS.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: NCHS reports 6.0% of US adults aged 18+ failed to obtain needed medical care due to cost in the 2025 NHIS early release.
prohibited_inferences: The measure identifies which treatment was missed.
The measure identifies the policy that caused the result.
The measure can be combined with the uninsured percentage into one rate.

counterevidence.statement: The measure does not identify a complete patient journey, a specific treatment, an outcome or a causal policy.

registered_falsifier.statement: The source-report claim fails if the frozen NCHS release, definition or correction does not reproduce 6.0% for adults aged 18+ in 2025.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Correct or withdraw the number if the frozen official release or a formal correction differs.
evidence_needed: Question wording, denominator and revision record

open_evidence_needs: Freeze the exact NCHS table and metadata because the public FastStats page can update.

claims.statement: The four-country healthcare observations establish one binding access condition for each country.

estimand.description: The condition that defeats every viable healthcare access route for a named person, service and period.

denominator.description: The retained sources use different people, services, waits, appointments, coverage measures and statistical units rather than a common access-journey denominator.

population.description: No common clinical-need population exists across the Spain, Belgium, Australia and United States observations.

geography.description: Separate non-harmonised national observations for Spain, Belgium, Australia and the United States.

time.description: The retained sources use different reference periods in 2024 and 2025-26 and do not form one comparison window.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: The official observations demonstrate that healthcare price, availability and proximity measures vary by service, person, provider, place and period and cannot be ranked on these denominators.
prohibited_inferences: The observations form a country ranking.
The observations identify the binding condition for a whole country.
The observations identify a named patient's binding condition.

counterevidence.statement: No common patient journey, service basket, clinical need, severity, waiting-time definition or cost denominator was found across all four countries.

registered_falsifier.statement: A binding-condition claim remains withdrawn unless the same named service, clinical-need population, viable routes, outcome standard and period are measured across the proposed comparison scope.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Do not publish a national binding-IF conclusion when any route, person, service, unit or period remains unmatched or unknown.
evidence_needed: Matched clinical need, eligibility, price, travel, wait, capacity and capability measures

open_evidence_needs: No harmonised four-country patient-journey dataset is retained; keep the example as a denominator lesson, not a comparison.

claims.statement: Consumer IFs and provider WHENs are the same conditions with a different verb.

estimand.description: Equivalence of condition nodes across affected-person outcome registers and actor-specific delivery or action registers.

denominator.statistical_unit: linked person-outcome and actor-work register pair
denominator.description: No set of independently encoded linked register pairs has been registered.

population.description: Relevant affected people and actors vary by service and are not sampled.

geography.description: No jurisdiction or service system has been fixed for an equivalence test.

time.description: No observation window has been fixed.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: Consumer and actor registers can contain causally linked but non-identical conditions.
prohibited_inferences: Changing IF to WHEN preserves condition identity.
Tense identifies a stable side of an exchange.
A consumer/provider binary captures funders, regulators, workers and mixed delivery systems.

counterevidence.statement: The draft's adjacent examples list consumer price, legality and reach but provider validation, licence and unit cost, directly demonstrating linked but non-identical registers.

registered_falsifier.statement: The identity claim remains withdrawn unless independent encoders applying preregistered equivalence rules recover the same condition nodes across person and actor registers without consequential omissions.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Use linked-register language if exact or functional equivalence falls below the preregistered threshold for any consequential condition class.

open_evidence_needs: Test linked-register mappings across mixed public, private and community delivery systems.

claims.statement: The Australian clerical-worker pilot is the first proof of the transition thesis.

estimand.description: Causal effect of AI adoption and work redesign on employment flows, earnings, essential access and experienced agency for scoped clerical workers.

denominator.statistical_unit: scoped clerical worker or preregistered cohort member
denominator.description: No linked worker cohort and outcome denominator has been established.

population.description: Candidate occupations are named, but a linked in-scope worker cohort is not established.

geography.description: Australia is proposed, with candidate states and SA4s conditional on data support.

time.description: No causal study period, baseline or follow-up window is registered.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: Australia has official building blocks for a bounded, prospective, no-consequence feasibility study.
prohibited_inferences: NERO movement is an observed AI effect.
Business AI use can be assigned to individual clerical workers or SA4s.
The retained sources establish displacement, essential-access loss, agency change or crisis.

counterevidence.statement: The retained sources measure different units and do not close the chain from occupational exposure through adoption and redesign to worker or household outcomes.

registered_falsifier.statement: Any future causal hypothesis fails if preregistered source-independent worker outcomes are better explained by macro-demand, sector composition, measurement change, policy/ownership or no-material-change models than by the AI pathway.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Retain feasibility-only status until a registered design separates the AI pathway from competing explanations and observes the protected outcomes in the same cohort.
evidence_needed: Common cohort, geography, classification and period

open_evidence_needs: Acquire one source-independent worker-flow outcome and one independently observed adoption or redesign event for the same registered cohort.

claims.statement: NERO publishes monthly modelled employment estimates for 355 four-digit occupations across 88 SA4 regions, and the estimates must not be summed or combined across occupations or geographies.

estimand.description: Publisher-modelled employment level for a specific four-digit occupation, SA4 residence region and release vintage.

denominator.description: A registered NERO cell, not a sum across occupations or geographies and not an individual worker record.

population.description: Employment represented by the NERO model for one of 355 four-digit occupations.

geography.description: One of 88 SA4 regions by worker residence, not business location.

time.description: Monthly estimate for a named source and release vintage.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: NERO reports this modelled estimate for this occupation, SA4 and vintage.
prohibited_inferences: The model cell is a direct employment observation.
A movement is caused by AI.
Smoothed estimates reliably detect rapid change outside model history.

counterevidence.statement: The series is experimental, smoothed, revision-prone, can miss rapid changes and shares source dependence with ABS Labour Force Survey inputs.

registered_falsifier.statement: The source-description claim fails if the frozen NERO release and methodology do not preserve the stated cell count, unit, non-additivity rule or modelled status.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Correct the register to the frozen vintage; never silently substitute current NERO metadata for the registered release.

open_evidence_needs: Freeze the exact NERO data and methodology artefacts for the proposed pilot vintage.

claims.statement: The ABS reports that 12% of in-scope businesses selected AI use in 2024-25.

estimand.description: Share of in-scope businesses reporting/selecting AI use under the ABS Characteristics of Australian Business question.

denominator.description: Businesses in the ABS survey population, not workers, jobs or tasks.

population.description: In-scope Australian businesses represented by the ABS survey.

geography.description: Australia national business estimate; not an SA4 worker estimate.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: Twelve per cent of in-scope businesses reported/select AI use in the 2024-25 ABS measure.
prohibited_inferences: Twelve per cent of workers use AI.
The statistic measures adoption intensity or task redesign.
The statistic identifies AI treatment for a clerical worker, occupation or SA4.

counterevidence.statement: The ABS item records selected business use, not intensity, task change, worker exposure, local adoption or individual treatment.

registered_falsifier.statement: The source-report claim fails if the frozen ABS release or question universe does not reproduce 12% for the stated business population and period.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Correct the value or scope to the frozen official release; do not reinterpret a changed question as the same series.

open_evidence_needs: Obtain an independently measured workplace adoption or task-redesign event before using this statistic in a worker-level transition chain.

claims.statement: A machine-readable repository boundary currently blocks public issuance or publication when review requirements fail.

estimand.description: Whether every operational route to public issuance is forced through an authenticated, non-bypassable validation and authorisation boundary.

denominator.description: No complete inventory of repository, CI, hosting, manual and alternate publication routes has been registered.

population.description: Callers and systems capable of preparing or publishing Observatory artefacts.

geography.description: The claim concerns technical and organisational control boundaries rather than a population geography.

time.description: Current repository and deployment state recorded on 2026-09-09.

inference_ceiling.permitted_statement: When invoked, repository validators can reject structurally incomplete candidate records under their declared checks.
prohibited_inferences: The library cannot be bypassed.
The repository authorises or blocks public publication.
A structurally valid packet has legitimate reviewers, authority, consent or evidence.

counterevidence.statement: The governance documents explicitly say a caller can bypass the library, no CI, hosting or operational issuance boundary exists, and the repository cannot authorise a public release.

registered_falsifier.statement: A future enforcement claim fails if any registered publication route can issue an artefact without authenticated review, valid authority and exact-byte checks enforced outside the caller-controlled library.
registered_falsifier.decision_rule: Describe the boundary as missing until a complete route inventory and adversarial bypass test show every consequential route fails closed.
evidence_needed: Externally enforced CI and hosting policy

open_evidence_needs: No operational issuance boundary exists; this requires external identity, CI, hosting and governance implementation beyond the repository validator.

evidence.claim_ceiling: Independent second-pass review findings and retained source ceilings; not a primary empirical source or truth determination.
The World Bank updated its 2021-PPP international, lower-middle-income and upper-middle-income lines to 3.00, 4.20 and 8.30 dollars in June 2025; 30 dollars is not one of those official lines.
PIP nowcasts are modelled estimates rather than direct current observations and require explicit threshold, PPP vintage, year and data vintage.
The retained processed World Bank-derived series reports 44.38% for the world in 2026 below 8.30 dollars per day in 2021 international dollars; it is not a direct observation or access measure.

The retained processed World Bank-derived series reports 80.04% for the world in 2026 below a user-set 30-dollar threshold in 2021 international dollars; it is not an official poverty line or audience measure.
Bounded healthcare source review preserving service, population, time and denominator differences; not a country ranking or binding-condition diagnosis.
CPS ASEC estimate of 27.1 million people, 8.0%, without health insurance coverage at any point during calendar year 2024; not affordability or service access among insured people.
The 2025 NHIS early release reports 6.0% of adults aged 18+ failed to obtain needed medical care due to cost; it does not identify treatment, outcome or cause.
Official Australian sources support a prospective no-consequence feasibility study but do not close the chain from AI capability to lived agency or establish a crisis.
Monthly modelled estimate for one of 355 four-digit occupations and one of 88 SA4 residence regions at a named vintage; not additive, a direct observation, rapid-change detector or causal AI measure.
Twelve per cent of in-scope businesses selected AI use in 2024-25; not intensity, task change, worker exposure or local worker treatment.
Modelled potential occupational exposure, with clerical occupations highest in the index; not Australian adoption, automation, displacement or harm.
The validator checks caller assertions and internal relationships; callers can bypass it and no CI, hosting or operational issuance boundary exists.
The repository cannot authorise a public release; the document specifies a missing boundary rather than claiming it exists.
